tanya rao: Hey team — my spouse just lost employer coverage in Germany and wants to enroll with our Redwood plan. Two quick Qs: 1) can we add them midyear as a QLE for loss of other coverage if the termination is overseas? 2) any carrier docs needed for non-US coverage loss (proof of prior coverage termination)? Also curious about whether HSA eligibility changes if we move from single to family midyear. Thanks!

olivia (People Ops): Sorry to hear that, @tanya. Short answer: yes, loss of other coverage (including employer coverage abroad) qualifies as a QLE. You'll need documentation showing the spouse's prior coverage ended — e.g., employer termination letter, final paystub showing insurance ended, or carrier proof of termination. If docs are in another language, a certified English translation is fine. Upload via: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/dependent-add and choose "Loss of Other Coverage".

people-ops-bot: Reminder: QLE window is 30 days from the date of loss of coverage. Submit evidence to avoid delays. See: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle-policy :information_source:

mike (Payroll): On HSA: if you switch from single to family midyear due to adding spouse, HSA contribution limits are pro-rated based on months of family coverage and IRS rules. Payroll will adjust pretax contributions accordingly and will flag potential excess contributions if you were already contributing toward the single limit. If you expect to change elections, DM payroll so we can project and avoid overcontribution.

olivia (People Ops): Carrier timing note: foreign documentation can slow carrier processing (7-21 business days). We can enroll immediately in the system with the requested effective date (usually the loss date or the date you request within the 30-day window); carriers will finalize once they process the proof. Payroll will prorate premiums from the coverage effective date and, if retro, may process a retro deduction or credit on the next pay run.

tanya rao: Great — I'll upload the German termination letter and spouse passport tonight. One more: does COBRA apply for EU employer plan or any special coordination?

olivia (People Ops): COBRA is a US statute so it won't apply to EU employer plans. For processing it's still treated as "loss of employer coverage" for our QLE rules. If the spouse has any portable coverage options from their EU employer, include details so we can advise on overlap or coordination.

mike (Payroll): If you request retro effective date back to the spouse's coverage end, expect a small retro deduction on the next payroll to catch up premiums. We'll include an itemized breakdown in Pay Details. If you'd like the deduction spread over two pay periods instead, reply here and we'll submit that request to payroll ops.

tanya rao: Thanks all — uploading now. Appreciate the quick help! :pray:
